info.bio: Gene Autry, (29 de septiembre de 1907 - 2 de octubre de 1998), es el más famoso de los cantantes cowboys de Hollywood. Su obra conocida se extiende desde 1929 hasta los años 1960 e incluye, junto a piezas ya olvidadas, un buen número de otras conocidas. En sus primeros trabajos abunda en el blues, siguiendo el estilo de su ídolo Jimmie Rodgers, y han sido parcialmente reeditados en Gene Autry : The blues singer (Columbia).

scenes.name: Antecedentes (1892-1950)
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Antes del rock'n'roll: Tin Pan Alley, los primeros discos de blues (Mamie Smith) y de «old-time music», el yodel de Jimmie Rodgers, el crooning de Bing Crosby, el boogie-woogie, el jump blues de Louis Jordan (nacimiento de facto del rhythm'n'blues), la guitarra jazzística de T-Bone Walker, Woody Guthrie como primer gran cantautor y la exótica de Les Baxter. En paralelo, la vanguardia clásica (Russolo, Satie, Varèse, Cage, Schaeffer) anticipa el ruido, el ambient y la electrónica.

podcast.title: Cowboy Movie Hero Archetype
podcast.body: Gene Autry was mentioned as an example of the cowboy movie heroes from Larry Weiss's youth, who were singers rather than actual ranchers, influencing the concept behind "Rhinestone Cowboy." "He was writing about the cowboy movie heroes of his youth, the Jean Autry types, who were singers, not ranchers."

podcast.title: Singing Cowboy Film Star
podcast.body: Gene Autry was a massive star during the 1930s and 40s, a period considered the heyday of singing cowboy films. His popularity contributed to the "Hollywoodization" of Western music, incorporating elements like crooning and orchestras. "But the 30s and 40s were the heyday of singing cowboy films with people like Gene Ortrie and Roy Rogers becoming massive, massive stars."

podcast.title: Western Music Star and Influence
podcast.body: Gene Autry was the preeminent Western music star during the late 1930s and early 1940s, and his influence extended to a wide range of musicians, including figures like Les Paul and Bo Diddley. His rendition of "Blueberry Hill" potentially inspired Fats Domino. "Ortrý...was the biggest Western music star at the late 30s and early 40s and influenced everyone from Les Paul to Bowie Didley."
